title: Finite morphisms are projective in the projective-bundle convention
statement: Let $h:T\to S$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then $h$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]: there is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module of finite type whose projective bundle contains $T$ as a closed subscheme over $S$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 29.43.2 (Tag 0B3I), morphisms-lemma-finite-projective, together with Definition 29.43.1 (Tag 01W8), clause (1) (projective means a closed immersion into a projective bundle).
